o.text: A derivation from Proto-Turkic *ül- (“to divide, distribute; lot, endowment”). Cognate with Turkmen and Turkish ülke, Bashkir өлкә (ülkä), Kyrgyz өлкө (ölkö), etc.
Borrowed from Arabic قُوَّة (quwwa). Doublet of qüvvət.
Borrowed from Arabic نَامُوس (nāmūs), ultimately from Ancient Greek νόμος (nómos).
From Proto-Turkic *bakačuk (“leg”, literally “little frog”). See more at Turkish bacak.
Borrowed from Russian библиомания (bibliomanija). By surface analysis, biblio- + -maniya.
